pcStatusOnce.consent: Windows YES (QR-v3 identity) + Windows STATUS (status) + Android QR signature consent + Android status consent
pcStatusOnce.lifetime: 1 use, QR expiry and <=90 seconds after QR-v3 identity

pcFileReceiveOnce.lifetime: single file, max 240 sec, QR expiration
pcFileReceiveOnce.consent: PC YES + Android QR proof + separate Windows SEND + Android file approval
pcFileReceiveOnce.hash: SHA-256 verified before Android Save As

privateDebugLab.status: private CI preview only; manual QA checklist, no PC/network API

pcFileUploadOnce.lifetime: single file, max 240 sec, QR expiration
pcFileUploadOnce.consent: PC YES + Android QR-v3 identity proof + separate Windows RECEIVE + separate Android upload approval
pcFileUploadOnce.hash: SHA-256 verified before temp+no-clobber link to PC owner-entered absolute NEW destination; temp cleanup on failure

privateDebugLab.status: private CI preview only; two-direction manual QA checklist, no privileged JS PC/network API

pcMediaOnce.mode: one key per freshly signed QR-v3 session
pcMediaOnce.consent: PC YES identity + new PC CONTROL (exact key) + Android identity proof + new Android media consent
pcMediaOnce.lifetime: max 90 seconds after PC extra approval, never past QR expiry

r6b.isolatedHttp: tools/test_pc_media_http.py, genuine P-256 test keys with mocked Windows media executor, loopback plain HTTP test-only
r6b.windowsMediaEmission: tools/test_pc_media_executor.py; stub user32 emits down/up exactly once; no real multimedia key issued in CI
r6b.concurrency: single successful signed request; rest denied; lost response/replay blocked
